chd.label: Campaign history 2017-2026
chd.portal: KP+TD UC spotting workbook (Dropbox, shared by EOC data cell)
chd.note: 134MB workbook; first read streams the DATA sheet into cache/ch_rows.pkl (~3 min), later runs reuse the cache until the workbook mtime changes.

can.label: Campaign analysis - district x campaign template rows
can.portal: KP+TD UC spotting workbook (Dropbox, shared by EOC data cell)
can.note: District-level aggregate of the same DATA sheet as chd: recorded missed NA/refusal, same-day covered, ICM missed + reasons and recall check/verified, market survey, LQAS pass/intermediate/fail, PCM clusters/checks/FM per campaign per district. Campaign order asserted against CHD.

snd.label: Upcoming campaign scope + day-wise targets
snd.portal: Final scope workbook issued for the upcoming campaign (D:\AMAZON DATA\SNID <campaign> folder)
snd.note: When a new campaign scope arrives, edit config.name and config.start here - the tab title, hero chip, countdown popup and Evening Review day dates all follow SND.n / SND.st. Rename the tab labels separately (search the old campaign name across the 4 variants).

ucc.label: UC criteria (EOC master categorization: Afghan bordering / core / endemic / high risk / rest of KP)
ucc.portal: EOC UC master categorization workbook (Master Sheet tab) - IDIMS + COMNet + EOC Cat blocks
ucc.note: One row per UC (1,402) with the EOC categorization blocks. Only the geo columns plus `Boardering UC` and `SKP/Rest KP` are read; COMNet staff names, PDA and IDIMS figures stay out of the payload. District categories are NOT taken from the workbook - they come from the dashboard's own `const SND` (the upcoming round's scope categories), so the criteria vocabulary follows the campaign. A UC flagged as bordering Afghanistan is labelled `Afghan bordering` even when its district sits in another category (8 UCs of KHYBER, 3 of WAZIR-N, 4 of WAZIR-S Lower). Districts outside the SND scope fall back to `Rest of KP`, asserted against the master's own SKP/Rest KP value. `al` carries legacy district spellings used by older payloads (combined WAZIR-S in CHD). Drop a newer Master Sheet into Downloads and run `--only ucc --force`. `aluc` repeats those Afghan-bordering UC names under legacy district names (config `legacy_afg`, incl. CHD spelling variants such as NIZAI NARAI) so rows recorded under the old combined WAZIR-S still tag as Afghan bordering.

fipv.label: fIPV Peshawar & Khyber scope (78 UCs)
fipv.portal: Peshawar & Khyber fIPV scope workbook + scope slide (Downloads)
fipv.note: Separate fIPV distribution plan for Peshawar and Khyber: 78 UCs, 1,184,376 children aged 4 months-10 years. The workbook supplies UC targets; the scope slide supplies the new/existing split and totals. Only the workbook is tracked for staleness - if the slide is revised run --only fipv --force.

icm.label: Intra-campaign monitoring (ICM) UC-wise sheet
icm.portal: EOC dashboard > Intra-campaign monitoring > export UC-wise sheet
icm.note: config.asof = null keeps the as-of date already embedded in the dashboard; set it (YYYY-MM-DD) when a new monitoring round is loaded.

pcm.label: Post-campaign monitoring (PCHS + PCM + ICM)
pcm.portal: PCHS household-check sheets + EOC post-campaign monitoring export (D:\AMAZON DATA), plus ICM columns of the KP+TD spotting workbook (reuses the chd cache)
pcm.note: One payload, three sources: the newest PCHS Data*.xlsx (campaign-wise household checks, currently Feb-Aug 2026), the newest POST CAMPAIGN MONITORING*.xlsx (currently SNID Sept-26) and per-UC ICM for the 2026 campaigns from the spotting workbook. Staleness tracks the newest matching file only - drop a new PCHS or PCM file into D:\AMAZON DATA and run --only pcm --force. When a campaign's post-campaign file arrives, it becomes the newest PCM dataset automatically. Surveyor names are never extracted (public site).

adv.label: ZD reported & covered 2024-2025 (IDIMS advance reports)
adv.portal: IDIMS > zero dose advance report > per-campaign UC export (all campaigns of a year in one file)
adv.note: Every advance_reports_*.xls under the roots is loaded - each file is self-contained, and a campaign present in several exports is taken from the newest file (so dropping a new year's file is enough). Staleness tracks only the newest file. Campaign names without a month/year go in config.campaigns; anything else unknown aborts the extract.

noc.label: NEOC intra-campaign monitoring exports (team visits, fixed sites, supervisor, transit)
noc.portal: NEOC > intra-campaign monitoring > team / fixed-site / transit / supervisor exports (CSV)
noc.note: Every icm_*.csv under Downloads is loaded; module comes from the filename (_supervisor/_fixed/_transit, plain = team visits), campaign from the Campaign name column. District names must match the dashboard spellings (ABOTABAD, BAR SWAT, ...). NEOC is login-gated - drop the CSV exports into Downloads and re-run.

novr.label: SNID campaign resource plan (district x team matrix)
novr.portal: EOC resource sheet issued with the campaign scope (D:\AMAZON DATA\SNID <campaign> folder)
novr.note: District-wise admin target + MT/SMT/CBV team matrix for the upcoming campaign, shown on the SNID Nov-26 scope tab. A new campaign resource plan csv anywhere under D:\AMAZON DATA becomes the newest source automatically; district names must match the Final Scope spellings (WAZIR-S Lower/Upper casing included).

mon.label: Monitor operations from LS 2026 Tableau workbooks (team + AIC monitoring)
mon.note: Scans every campaign folder; maps ActivityName to dashboard cq labels. Surveyor Email used for distinct counts only, never embedded. Stale duplicate folders (KP-Special-1-Jul = May byte-copy) are skipped.

icmq.label: Intra-campaign monitoring quality (team monitored + AIC visited, UC level)
icmq.portal: EOC dashboard > Intra-campaign monitoring > export UC-wise (team-monitored and AIC-visited tables)
icmq.note: One CSV per table; the "2 campaigns" exports carry the newest campaign (SNID Sept 2026) with a slightly different column set, the big exports carry the full 2021-2026 history. District x campaign aggregates are count-weighted means rounded to whole percent; -1 = indicator absent from that export. 'Total' rows are skipped. The AIC 2-campaign export has no supervisor count column, so those rows are averaged per UC (wt.aic = "uc").

neap.label: Upcoming campaign pre-campaign readiness (NEAP district-wise status)
neap.portal: EOC dashboard > Campaign > Pre Campaign > NEAP readiness (district wise)

web.note: Login-gated (plain HTTP redirects to /login). In the signed-in portal click Export to Excel on each page (table2excel filename NEAP); _refresh/neap_auto.py picks the newest NEAP*.xls from Downloads and republishes on a schedule.

neap.note: Fourteen readiness columns per district (DPEC in time, DC/DHO, must-members, UCMO, UC secretary, AICs trained, teams trained, microplans validated, members 18+, local / govt / female member, inaccessible areas). The portal re-saves the same file under a " (n)" counter and mixes two shapes: district-wise (~35 KB) and UC-wise (Province/District/Tehsil/UC before the same 14 indicators, emitted as `u`). Whatever the newest save is, the district payload is read from the newest district-wise file and `u` from the newest UC-wise file; older-shape neapreport*/allneapreport* exports are excluded by pattern. District names must match the SND scope or the extractor aborts.

nact.label: SNID Nov-26 activity countdown calendar (planned timeline)
nact.portal: PEOC/NEOC countdown-of-SNIDs activity calendar issued before each round
nact.note: Manual Gantt grid: day numbers in row 2 (C..AC = Oct 5..31, AD..AS = Nov 1..16), activities 1-28 in rows 4..31, windows as cell fills (accent4 main, FF00B0F0 secondary, FFFF0000 post-campaign reviews, accent2 catch-up/LQAS days, accent6 campaign week; white + orange = grid base/Sundays). Merged notes inside the grid ride as activity notes. The B1 header supplies title/vaccine/dates; the campaign month is asserted against auto.snd.config.start so a stale calendar cannot land after the scope moves to the next round.

ind.label: Compiled campaign indicators (Admin, ICM, market survey, LQAS, PCM)
ind.portal: EOC dashboard compiled campaign indicators export (2017-2026, 85 campaigns)
ind.note: One row per UC per campaign (84 columns, 75,792 rows). The payload carries district aggregates for every campaign plus the raw UC rows of the 2025+ campaigns, so the five dashboard tables offer a district / UC toggle. Percent columns are recomputed from their count pairs; Same Day coverage and ICM Seen % have no count pair and are stored as the district mean of UC values. A literal -1 in the source counts as not reported, other negatives are kept. Keep the payload under refresh.py's 5 MB size ceiling - if the next export adds more UC-detail years, raise UC_FROM_YEAR or the ceiling.

inda.label: Admin coverage and missed children for SNID Sept 2026 (const INDA)
inda.portal: EOC summary coverage report (portal > coverage > export UC-wise), saved by the legacy pipeline as cov_SNID Sept 2026.xls
inda.note: Fills the Sept-2026 gap in the compiled-indicators export: the data pack's Admin table gets SNID Sept 2026 from the same UC-wise coverage workbook as the Missed children tab. Only admin coverage/missed columns are available; MP target, same-day coverage, guest, HRMP mobile and school stay not reported. Drop the new coverage export into _portal and run --only inda --force.

epm.label: EPI month index (EMETA) with the 2024/2025 monthly exports
epm.note:
Every single-month export's own period header (
YYYY-MM - YYYY-MM
) is read; per-district aggregates are cached in _refresh/cache/epi25mon.pkl keyed by file id, so only new files pay the pandas parse. Months already embedded in index.html (2026) are kept; parsed months are added. Run together with epim.

epim.label: EPI district-month coverage rows (EPIM) with 2024-2025
epim.note: Companion to epm (same parse cache). pre-2026 district rows are aggregated from the monthly exports (2025 UC-wise, 2024 district-level); the embedded 2026 rows are kept verbatim; an EPI district not in the embedded mapping aborts the extract.

rca.label: EPI-MIS rapid coverage assessments, visit-level (const ERCA)
rca.note: Every RCA_Report*.xls is loaded (each export covers its own date range); month x district aggregates are cached per file id (_refresh/cache/rcamon.pkl). Newest file wins per month x district. Monitor names/IDs/designations are never extracted (public site). RCA_Report (36).xls (16-Oct-2026) is a NATIONAL export (GB/Punjab/Sindh/ICT districts, 593 rows) that is not the KP series - excluded in sources.json.

esup.label: EPI supervisory checklist visits, fixed + outreach (const ESUP)
esup.note: Every Supervisory_Checklist_Report*.xls is loaded (2026 arrives as two exports: fixed-site and outreach). Newest file wins per month x district x site type; per-file cache in _refresh/cache/esumon.pkl. Monitor names/CNICs/designations are never extracted (public site).

zd.label: ZD Digitization (IDIMS comparison report)
zd.portal: IDIMS / SMC Tracker > Comparison Report export
zd.howto: Drop the newest Comparison_Report_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx into BOTH D:\AMAZON DATA and C:\Users\HD\Downloads (the legacy pipeline scans Downloads), then rebuild and harvest - see SOURCES.md, 'Harvesting from the legacy pipeline'. DATA needs two reports: the newest one plus the latest one from a DIFFERENT campaign, which supplies the rp/lp comparison columns. Never run zd_refresh.py against this repo - it rebuilds from dashboard_template.html and would drop every tab added after 10-Oct-2026.

zdcov.label: ZD Reported & Covered (multi-campaign coverage workbook)
zdcov.portal: IDIMS > zero dose reported/covered export, one per campaign, saved as _portal\cov_<campaign>.xls in the legacy folder
zdcov.howto: Update D:\AMAZON DATA\ZERO DOSE REPORTED AND COVERED.xlsx and/or drop new cov_<campaign>.xls overlays into C:\Users\HD\Downloads\ZD_Dashboard\_portal, then rebuild and harvest (see SOURCES.md). ZD is NOT produced by the Comparison Report - do not confuse it with the zd entry above.

val.label: ZD Validation (child-level app export)
val.portal: SMC Tracker form 200 > combined export (login required)
val.howto: Save the combined CSV export as C:\Users\HD\Downloads\ZD_Dashboard\_portal\val_<campaign>.csv (move the previous copy into _portal\_prev). Each val_*.csv REPLACES every master row of the campaigns it contains, so keep one file per campaign. Then rebuild and harvest (see SOURCES.md). VCH is the only payload that differs per variant: the internal build carries nm/fn plus real cd/mo, the public build drops nm and fn and blanks cd and mo. Derive the public one from the internal one - never copy either way blindly. Do NOT mirror these CSVs into the repo's own _portal folder: it is published on GitHub Pages and they carry child names, father names, EPI card numbers, monitor names and surveyor emails.

epi.label: Routine EPI coverage (UC YTD + district monthly)
epi.howto: EMETA/EPIM now refresh automatically (auto.epm + auto.epim). The UC-level EPI payload (const EPI, Jan-Sep 2026 YTD) is still rebuilt with _pipeline\_epi_jansep_patch.py in the legacy folder and injected here until 2026 monthly exports exist.

cq.label: Campaign quality / intra-campaign operational indicators
cq.howto: Export from NEOC into _portal/camp_quality.json, or use the in-dashboard NEOC import block on the Intra-campaign tab (stores to localStorage, never to the repo).

mism.label: Missed children & refusals
mism.portal: EOC dashboard > per-campaign coverage export (login required)
mism.howto: Save one coverage export per campaign as _portal\cov_<campaign>.xls (the .xls is really an HTML table), then rebuild and harvest. Not derived from the val_*.csv validation exports - those feed the val entry.

surv.label: Surveillance (AFP + district surveillance)
surv.howto: Refresh the _portal JSON exports, then rebuild SURVM/AFP.

neoc.label: NEOC operational indicators (AIC visited, teams monitored)
neoc.howto: In-dashboard import only: Intra-campaign tab > NEOC block > paste table / import CSV-TSV-HTML export / run the copied snippet in your own NEOC console. Stored in localStorage['kpNEOC.icm.v1'], never committed. Session cookies are not used by any script here.
